ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A uniform electric field has a field strength of $40\mathrm{N/C}$. There are two points, A and B, on the same electric field line. A particle with a mass of $2\times10^{{-}9}\mathrm{kg}$ and a charge of $-\ 2\times10^{{-}9}\mathrm{C}$ is moved from point A to point B, and the electrostatic force performs $1.5\!\times\!10^{-7}\mathrm{J}$ of positive work.

1. Determine the electric potential difference $U_{AB}$ between points A and B.
2. If the particle has an initial velocity of $10\mathrm{m/s}$ in the same direction as the electric field line at point A, calculate its velocity at point B under the influence of only the electrostatic force.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$-75\mathrm{V}$
$5\sqrt{10}\mathrm{m/s}$, direction aligned with the electric field lines

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A uniform electric field has a field strength of $40\mathrm{N/C}$. There are two points, A and B, on the same electric field line. A particle with a mass of $2\times10^{-9}\mathrm{kg}$ and a charge of $-2\times10^{-9}\mathrm{C}$ is moved from point A to point B, and the electrostatic force performs $1.5\times10^{-7}\mathrm{J}$ of positive work. 1. Determine the electric potential difference $U_{AB}$ between points A and B. 2. If the particle has an initial velocity of $10\mathrm{m/s}$ in the same direction as the electric field line at point A, calculate its velocity at point B under the influence of only the electrostatic force.
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: $-75\mathrm{V}$ $5\sqrt{10}\mathrm{m/s}$, direction aligned with the electric field lines
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: No image evidence is needed because the problem is text-only. Given work by the electrostatic force from A to B is W_AB=+1.5×10^-7 J and charge q=-2×10^-9 C. Using the electrostatic work-potential relation W_AB=q U_AB, where U_AB=V_A−V_B, we get U_AB=W_AB/q=(1.5×10^-7)/(-2×10^-9)=-75 V. For the velocity, use the work-energy theorem over A to B: K_B−K_A=W_AB. The initial kinetic energy is K_A=(1/2)mv_0^2=(1/2)(2×10^-9)(10^2)=1.0×10^-7 J. Thus K_B=1.0×10^-7+1.5×10^-7=2.5×10^-7 J. Since K_B=(1/2)mv_B^2=(1×10^-9)v_B^2, v_B^2=(2.5×10^-7)/(1×10^-9)=250, so v_B=√250=5√10 m/s. For the direction, the motion is constrained to the same field line: the initial velocity is along the field line and the electrostatic force is collinear with that field line, so the velocity at B remains along the field line.
